events.text: Request filed.

The District answered in writing: no well applications near the Southland mill site in the past two years and no contact with Amp Z or Verdant. It disclosed that WattBridge was approved in late 2024 and early 2025 for wells totaling 80 million gallons a year for a power plant in the north of the county, never drilled, and in March 2026 asked for 1.5 billion gallons a year for a 24/7 plant; that request has been on hold since July 2026 at the company's request. The District asked whether ETLC still wanted the documents and requested until Oct. 16 to gather them.
ETLC confirmed it still wants the WattBridge permit applications and the related board agendas and minutes, and dropped the rig supply well applications.

The District sent board agendas and minutes from Aug. 5, 2024 (Angelina WSC) and Feb. 10, 2025 (WattBridge). It said WattBridge never drilled its two approved wells, so no permits were issued, and that the later 1.5-billion-gallon request came mostly by phone with no board meeting or public hearing. The District expects to send the rest by Nov. 9.

The District said it will try to finish all of ETLC's requests by Nov. 9 and asked for one list of the records still needed. ETLC sent it the same day: the WattBridge applications and any records of its 1.5-billion-gallon request, and the Hudson Water Supply well records.

The District said it is struggling to meet Nov. 9 because of unexpected public comments for its Nov. 9 rules hearing, and that records may come a piece at a time because its email cannot send large or multiple attachments. ETLC replied the same day asking for whatever is ready now, offering a zip file, a share link or smaller emails, and promising to confirm receipt by file name.

The District's Nov. 9 date passed with no records sent. ETLC sent a written past-due notice asking for the records, or a written date and hour they will be available, by Nov. 13, and said it will file a complaint with the Nacogdoches County prosecutor under Gov't Code 552.3215 if nothing comes.

No records arrived by Nov. 9. ETLC sent a written past-due notice asking for everything ready by end of day Nov. 13, and for anything not ready, a written date and hour under Gov't Code 552.221. The District replied the same day that it will send as much as it can by Nov. 13 and say when to expect the rest. ETLC confirmed it will expect the records by Nov. 13 and asked the District to confirm the notice was shared with its Board.
The District said it has shared ETLC's past-due notice with its Board of Directors.

ETLC wrote that no records or written date had arrived after the District's Nov. 10 promise to send what it could by Nov. 13. ETLC set a final date of Nov. 25 to send the records or certify a date and hour for each, and said it will file a complaint under Gov't Code 552.3215 if neither arrives.

The District sent 35 files: permits A0046-A0048 issued to Paluxy LandCo for three wells at 3641 Ben Dunn Road (13 million gallons a year combined), the application and email records for that site, the original WattBridge applications, the Feb. 10, 2025 board agenda and minutes, and District well and pumping data. found: No one has applied to drill wells near the old Southland mill in the past two years, and the District says it has had no contact with Amp Z or Verdant Industries.

events.text: Request emailed to the City Secretary.
The City logged the request as CRR-2026-366.

The City sent a cost estimate of $464.94 (25.83 hours of staff time at $15 an hour plus 20% overhead) and asked for a $232.47 deposit within 10 business days, by Dec. 4. The estimate includes 1.5 hours of City Secretary time for "review and redaction."

ETLC answered the cost estimate in writing the same evening (Gov't Code 552.2615(b)): it modified the request to take records the City already keeps electronically and a vendor payment history instead of scanned paper invoices, asked the City to drop the 1.5 hours of "review" time (1 TAC 70.3(d)(3) bars charging for deciding what to withhold), and asked for a public-interest fee waiver under 552.267. ETLC asked for a revised estimate.

The City sent a revised estimate of $328.14 and asked for a $164.07 deposit within 10 business days. It said staff found about 55 contracts that may be responsive and would print payment histories for about 51 vendors instead of copying paper invoices.
